The first run sent 105 pages to Azure (46%) and verified 440 values; the table shows the result after the fixes.

**Scanned pages are the remaining Azure load.** A free local second reader is queued next to address it (docs/overnight-report.md, follow-ups).

## Exact characters from embedded text, with Vision's layout (2026-10-09)

Apple's default `--use-text-layer auto` keeps Vision's blocks (layout, tables, margin numbers, Bates) and aligns each block's words with the PDF's embedded text inside the block's box. A new bridge call, `ocr_bridge_text_in_regions`, inverts the render transform and works on rotated pages. The alignment is in `src/embedded.rs`. Its safeguards:
- **Page gate:** at least 90% word agreement on the page, or nothing changes.
- **Per-word check:** a differing word is replaced only when it looks like a misread, with at most a third of its characters different.
- **No inserted text:** embedded text that Vision did not see is never added. This covers redactions, hidden text, and neighbours caught by a box.
- **Skipped for now:** column-split and transcript pages.

Measured on the 20 public filings (230 pages, Apple, 150 DPI), against the earlier pure-OCR run:

| | Pure OCR | Default `auto` |
|---|---|---|
| Born-digital pages corrected | - | 95 of 139 |
| Partly born-digital pages corrected | - | 13 of 28 |
| Words changed to the embedded form | - | 1,350 |
| Output words found in the embedded text (born-digital) | 90.1% | 90.7% |
| Output words found in the embedded text (partial) | 98.0% | 98.4% |
| `--verify-json` pages in `azure_pages` | 61 | 51 |
| Of which e-filed / partial / scanned | 18 / 9 / 34 | 15 / 2 / 34 |
| Values verified free | 576 | 601 |

**The word-match share is a weak metric here,** because it rises only a little. Vision's own output carries margin numbers and headers that the embedded text orders or spells differently, and the 44 uncorrected born-digital pages are either column-split or transcript pages, or below the 90% page gate.

**Sample corrections:**
- `Califomia` to `California`;
- `SZA` to `S2A` (a company name);
- `S10` and `S8` to `$10` and `$8`;
- `mıkulicm(@)sec.gov` to `mikulicm@sec.gov`;
- straight quotes to the filing's curly quotes.

**Goldens:** the pure-OCR goldens (`--use-text-layer never`) are byte-identical apart from the new empty `embedded_text_fixes: {}` line. A new test checks the default output on legal.pdf: the golden with `Case No.3:26-cv-04417` corrected to `Case No. 3:26-cv-04417`.

## `--verify-json` compares values, not substrings (2026-10-09)

A review found that `verified` meant "the squashed text occurs somewhere in the embedded text", so `$3,000` was verified by `$3,000,000` and `3:26-cv-0441` by `3:26-cv-04417`. Now each field and the embedded text are reduced to the same canonical keys:
- amount in cents;
- ISO date;
- docket as office, year, kind and number;
- squashed text for Bates numbers and citations.

A field is `verified` only when its key is among the embedded text's keys. The embedded text is flattened first, so a date or amount broken across lines still matches. Docket keys also match without the office prefix.

**Look-alike characters:** amounts, dates and dockets that mix digits with `O o I l S B Q` get `confusable_characters` and no `value`. They are never verified. An error-injection test plants 16 misreads into a page whose embedded text has the true values: look-alike letters, one-digit changes, and `$3,000` for `$3,000,000`. It checks that none comes back `verified`.

**Scale words:** `$45` at the end of a line followed by `million` on the next (past one blank line or a pleading line number) is the amount `$45 million`. `K`/`M`/`B` suffixes are scales. `$1,50B` stays a malformed amount.

Measured on the 20 public filings (Apple, default `auto`), against the substring check:

| | Substrings | Values |
|---|---|---|
| Pages in `azure_pages` | 51 | 53 |
| Values verified free | 601 | 602 |
| No longer verified | - | 3 |
| Newly verified | - | 4 |

**The three values no longer verified:**
- `CV-00886` twice: a false Bates match (the text is part of a docket number);
- `$246.95` on a scanned loan form, where the embedded text has `246 95` with the cents in a separate box.

Both outcomes are the safe direction. The newly verified values are amounts whose scale word was on the next line.

## Second reader for scanned pages (2026-10-09)

`--verify-json` now reads each page that has values but no embedded text a second time. The bridge gained a `reader: "text"` option. It runs Vision's older `RecognizeTextRequest` (line level, accurate, no language correction) at 300 DPI, and returns lines with confidence and the next-best readings. Two re-reads run at a time, within the bridge's Vision limit.

**Confidence and alternatives carry no signal in accurate mode.** On 732 lines of a scanned motion, confidence was 1.0 on every line, and no line had an alternative. The doubtful check (confidence below 0.5, or a next-best reading that changes the value) is kept because it costs nothing, but in practice it does not fire.

**Measured blind on born-digital pages.** The pages were OCRed with `--use-text-layer never`, and the embedded text was hidden from verify (`OCR_VERIFY_IGNORE_EMBEDDED=1`), so the second reader decided alone. Its decisions were graded against the run that could see the embedded text. 20 public filings, 230 pages:

| | Values |
|---|---|
| Values the embedded text confirms | 574 |
| Of these, flagged by the second reader (false alarms) | 27 (4.7%) |
| Values the embedded text contradicts | 47 |
| Of these, flagged by the second reader | 21 (45%) |

**Agreement between two Apple readings proved not independent.** Before agreement was demoted, 546 values were confirmed this way, and 25 of them disagreed with the embedded text. Most of those 25 were cases where the embedded text was itself wrong or misparsed:
- a 1985 scan with an old OCR text layer;
- a handwritten form;
- a footnote marker stuck to an amount, `$1,000,000.8`.

Eight were real shared errors. A Jane Street filing carries two overprinted stamps, `Filed 04/24/24` and `Filed 04/18/24`, and both Apple readers read the blend as `04/28/24`, a date in neither stamp.

**Hence:** on Apple pages the second reading only finds disagreements. Agreement verifies a value only when the first reading came from a model engine, and the page did not fall back to Apple.

**Symbol repair:** the second reading gets the same `§`/`¶` restoration as the first. Without it, `S 1983` was a disagreement with `§ 1983`. Restoring the symbols cut false alarms from 46 to 27, and catches went from 22 to 21. Bare pleading line numbers are dropped before matching, because they come between `May 7,` and `2007.`. `S5,500` counts as `$5,500` when the amount has digit grouping or cents.

**Default run** (Apple, `auto`, 20 filings), compared with master:
- **Pages in `azure_pages`:** 53 → 55. Nine values on scans are now `check` rather than `unchecked`. Three of them are `§` misread as `$` (`$1446`, `$ 1983`, `$2254`).
- **Time:** 125 s → 144 s for the whole set; 60 pages were re-read.

**Not yet measured:** a live model run. The model path (agreement verifies) is unit-tested only.

## Whole-text agreement (2026-10-09)

`--verify-json` now reports, per page, which sentences another reading has word for word (`text_agreement`, `src/agreement.rs`). This tells a tool which wording it can quote.
- **Spans:** sentences, or whole lines when shorter. Abbreviations like `No.`, `U.S.C.` and `Inc.` do not end a sentence.
- **Comparison:** words are compared as letters and digits, case-insensitively, in order, and with nothing between them.

Each rule below came from a failure on the public filings, or from the error-injection test, which changes, drops or doubles every word of a reference passage in turn:
- **Pleading line numbers** may be skipped, but only structurally:
  - in the other reading, when they stand alone on a line or start one;
  - in the Markdown, only at the start of a line.

  A number inside a line is never skipped, so `30` read for `80` still differs, and so does a `30` that only the OCR has. That matters because a model can invent a number.
- **Edges:** in prose (a span ending in sentence punctuation), the span must start and end at a sentence or line edge of the other reading. A span that follows another sentence in the Markdown must follow a sentence end there too. Without this, a sentence missing its first word ("Not later than…" read as "later than…") agreed, and so did a doubled `2024.` at a line start. Headers and table cells are exempt, because Vision splits them where the PDF has one line.
- **Margin legends:** PDFKit puts the vertical left-margin legend ("United States District Court / Northern District of California") between a paragraph's lines. A whole line of the other reading may be skipped inside a match only if it has at least three words, and the Markdown has it on another line. A line the OCR dropped is not elsewhere in the Markdown, so it still breaks agreement (tested).

**Measured on the 20 public filings** (Apple, default `auto`):

| Pages | Compared with | Sentences agreed | Median words agreed per page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Born-digital (139) | embedded text | 77.2% | 90% |
| Partly born-digital (28) | embedded text | 91.4% | 94% |
| Scanned (59) | second Apple reading, not independent | 64.6% | 64% |

**What remains unagreed on born-digital pages:**
- real differences: OCR misreads (`Issu`, `It'l`) on pages the embedded correction does not touch;
- a 1985 scan whose text layer is itself bad OCR, and a handwritten form;
- condensed two-up transcripts, whose layout the PDF text orders differently.

All of these are the safe direction: a sentence that does not agree is not quoted as confirmed.

## Missing-text check (2026-10-09)

`text_agreement.missing_lines` lists the lines of the other reading (embedded text, or the second reader) that the OCR lacks entirely. A page with at least 5 such words gets `missing_text` in `page_check`.

**What counts as missing:** a line with at least 4 words, of which fewer than a third of the word pairs appear anywhere in the page's Markdown. A misread word spoils at most two pairs, so lines with OCR errors are not taken for missing ones.

**How the rule was reached:**
- The first rule was "no three-word run in common". It flagged 106 pages, because short lines with one misread (`prepare a detense.`) lost every run.
- Letter-spaced headings (`A P P E A R A N C E S`) are joined into one word.
- An error-injection test drops each line of a page in turn: each is reported, and the full page reports nothing.

**Measured on the 20 public filings** (Apple, default `auto`):
- **Pages with `missing_text`:** 88, of which 57 born-digital, 13 partly born-digital, and 18 scanned (against the second reader).
- **Spread:** more than a third of them are on two documents. One is a 1985 loan note whose text layer is itself bad OCR, which matches nothing (10 pages). The other is a bankruptcy filing whose "Created with Scanner Pro" stamp the OCR garbles on every page (15).
- **Real drops:** spot checks found Apple Vision skipped whole visible text.
  - On a two-column dealer agreement, the "ARTICLE NINTH: Execution of Agreement" paragraph is plainly printed and absent from the OCR.
  - On an order, a footnote citation (`278 F.Supp.2d 1079`) is missing.
- **Azure cost:** `azure_pages` went from 55 to 57. Born-digital pages with `missing_text` get `second_reading: embedded_text` when their values match, because the PDF's own text is the free second reading.

**Not yet measured:** precision over the whole set. It needs a labelled sample of flagged lines; the eval item in the queue will add it.

## Arithmetic checks (2026-10-09)

`src/arithmetic.rs` adds two checks to `--verify-json`. A mismatch adds its reason to `page_check` and to the amount fields involved. No value is ever changed.

**Amounts in words against numerals**, for example `Three Hundred Ninety Two Dollars and Thirty One Cents ($392.31)`, `four million dollars ($4 million)`, or `FORTY-FIVE THOUSAND AND NO/100 DOLLARS ($45,000.00)`.
- The words must name money (`dollars`, `cents`, `NN/100`), so `Section Two ($500 per day)` is not compared.
- An error-injection test changes a digit on either side, or a number word, and each change is caught.

**Table totals:** a row labelled total must equal the sum of the money cells above it in the same column, back to the header or the previous total.
- A `Subtotal` row is allowed for: the next total may equal the subtotals plus the rows after them (tax, fees).
- Cells count as money only with `$`, digit grouping or cents, so years and counts are not summed.
- An injection test changes each line item, and then the total; each change is caught.

**Public filings:** no mismatches. The two amounts in words in the set (`four million dollars ($4 million)` and `Three Hundred Ninety Two Dollars and Thirty One Cents ($392.31)`) agree with their numerals, and no table has a total row whose sum fails. Both checks are therefore exercised mostly by the synthetic tests.

## More case-number formats, and money without `$` (2026-10-09)

**Labelled case numbers:** the token after `Case No.`, `Civil Action No.`, `C.A. No.`, `Index No.`, `Cause No.` or `Adv. Proc. No.` is a docket field, in any court's format: `11-4604 PSG`, `C-08-01337 MHP`, `5215-VCG`, `20 Civ. 05382`, `651234/2021`.
- **Excluded:** `Docket No. 35` (an entry citation).
- **Matching:** these are compared as their exact letters and digits. A look-alike letter in a digit run (`C-O8-01337`) is still found, and gets `confusable_characters`.
- **Fragments:** a number cut off at a line end (`Case No. 03:11-`) is dropped, and so is anything with fewer than four digits. On the public filings, such fragments (`03:11`, `5:19`) had matched equally cut-off fragments in the embedded text.

**Money without `$`:** `USD 5,000`, `5,000 dollars`, and `sum|amount|total|price|fee|payment|balance of 5,000.00`. Cents are required in the last shape, because "amount of 1,500 units" is a count. These are compared by value with `$` amounts.

**Embedded text:** a hyphen at a line end now joins its halves before values are read (`5:15-` / `CV-01102-JGB-SP`), and soft hyphens are dropped. Without this, two correctly read case numbers were flagged.

**Public filings:**
- 23 more docket fields: 15 verified, 3 `unchecked` (on scans), and 5 `check`.
- One of the `check` values is a real disagreement: the OCR reads `5:15CV-01102-JGB` where the page has `5:15-CV-01102-JGB-SP`, a dropped hyphen.
- No amounts without `$` occur in the set, so that shape is exercised by tests only.

**Not done:** embedded-text correction on column-split and transcript pages. That changes the OCR text itself, and would need its own measurement against the Jev judge.

## Verification eval: Apple and paddleocr-vl (2026-10-09)

`eval/verify_eval.py` grades `--verify-json` on the 167 public-filing pages that have embedded text. The PDF's own text is the reference, and each engine is scanned twice: as users run it, and with the embedded text hidden from verify. paddleocr-vl numbers are from the build before the `¶` look-alike fix below. Apple numbers include it.

| | Apple | paddleocr-vl |
|---|---|---|
| Field precision / recall / F1 vs embedded text | 93.3% / 78.3% / 85.1% | 85.9% / 89.8% / 87.8% |
| Word error rate vs embedded text (order-sensitive) | 38.2% | 36.9% |
| Pages to Azure, normal run | 58 | 64 |
| Hidden-text run: `verified` by the second reader | 0 (agreement not independent) | 590, 23 wrong (3.9%) |
| Hidden-text run: misread values caught as `check` | 27 of 29 (93%) | 54 of 77 (70%) |
| Hidden-text run: false alarms from the value itself | 5.7% | 20.3% |
| Hidden-text run: false alarms including page checks | 34.5% | 20.3% |
| Sentences agreed by model and Vision, not in the embedded text | n/a | 126 of 3,531 (3.6%) |

**The 23 wrong `verified` values for paddleocr-vl:**
- **The embedded text is wrong or misparsed in 15.** These are on the 1985 note, the handwritten Nissan form, and the footnote marker in `$1,000,000.8`.
- **The other 8 are one real shared error.** The overprinted Jane Street stamp (`04/24/24` over `04/18/24`) reads `04/28/24` to the model and to Vision alike. In normal use, that page's embedded text catches it (`not_in_embedded_text`). On a true scan nothing would: overprinted or doubled stamps are a residual risk that no pair of image readers removes.

**The 126 sentences agreed but not in the embedded text** are, in the sample read, comparison artifacts rather than wrong wording:
- a running header (`SEC v. KUZDAS ET AL.`) that the PDF text places mid-line;
- leading pleading numbers;
- transcript cells.

So 3.6% is an upper bound.

**False alarms:** paddleocr-vl's are mostly a scanner stamp that Vision garbles (45 on one filing), and `¶` read as `"1`, `9|` or `11` (34). The `¶` look-alikes are now matched in the second reading. The number must still be equal. Apple's page-level false alarms come from `missing_text` between two Apple readings, whose line coverage differs.

## Embedded-text correction on column-split and transcript pages (2026-10-09)

`--use-text-layer auto` now also corrects column-split and transcript pages. On a transcript, the mini-pages' Vision lines are corrected before their numbers are re-anchored. Getting this right took five fixes, each found on the public filings or the fixtures:

1. **Exact character selection.**
   - **The problem:** PDFKit's `selection(for: rect)` selects like a mouse drag, from the first character to the last in text order. On a 2-up or 4-up transcript, or two columns, a box takes in the neighbouring column's lines (`itigation`, `hat`). The transcript locator's mini-page rectangles are also rough: "page 9" spanned 72% of a 4-up sheet.
   - **Now:** for column-split and transcript pages, the bridge takes exactly the characters whose centre lies in the box, spaced by their positions (`geometric`). `characterBounds(at:)` counts characters differently from `page.string`, so a one-character selection's bounds are used.
   - **Ordinary pages** keep PDFKit's selection. Their alignment was already measured, and footnote superscripts fall outside a block's geometric box.
2. **A dash is not a broken word.** `embedded_words` joined `--` with the next word as if it were a line-end hyphen, which made `-- -well`. This also happened on master: 6 words on one deposition.
3. **Short words on these pages change only between look-alikes** (`l`/`I`/`|`, `O`/`0`, Cyrillic `А`/`A`). Misalignment in transcript tables had turned line number `7` into `6`, `Page 30` into `Page 3`, and `of` into `o`.
4. **Re-splits keep what Vision read.** A re-split must keep all of Vision's characters, though punctuation it missed may come back: `14lawsuit` / `14 lawsuit`, and `units essentially,` / `units—essentially,`, but not `--14` / `14`. An aligned word glued to punctuation keeps it (`Document#:` / `Document #:`).
5. **Invisible OCR layers are not corrections.** The two filings with bad text layers (the 1985 note and the handwritten dealer form) draw all their text in render mode 3. A new bridge call counts text-showing operators by render mode. A page that is mostly invisible text is not corrected.

**Measured on the 20 public filings** (Apple, default), against master:

| | Master | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Column-split and transcript pages corrected | 0 | 25 (167 words) |
| Ordinary pages corrected | 109 (1,350 words) | 103 (1,313 words) |
| Transcript pages whose numbers cannot be re-anchored | 27 | 27 |
| Pages in `azure_pages` / values verified | 58 / 618 | 57 / 619 |

The six fewer ordinary pages are on the two OCR-layer filings. Their layer was sometimes better than Vision (`agreed`, `Illinois`) and sometimes worse (`provislons`), so it is no longer applied as if it were exact.

**Fixtures:**
- The 4-up transcript fixture goes from 741 to 743 of 745 expected words, with all line numbers still anchored. The fixes are `guality` → `quality` and `$68, 973.00` → `$68,973.00`.
- A new fixture, `spike/fixtures/ocr_layer.pdf` (`spike/make_ocr_layer.py`), lays an invisible misspelled layer over a scanned image. Without the check the output takes `qction` and `Cqurt`; with it, nothing changes.

## Invisible OCR layers in `--verify-json` (2026-10-09)

The embedded-text correction already skips pages whose text is drawn invisibly. `--verify-json` now treats such pages the same way:
- each page gets `ocr_text_layer`;
- a value's agreement with the layer verifies nothing, while a disagreement is `not_in_ocr_text_layer` (`check`);
- text agreement is reported as `compared_with: ocr_text_layer`, not independent;
- a suspect page goes to Azure, never to "read the embedded text".

**Public filings:**

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Values verified free | 619 | 499 |
| Values on the two OCR-layer filings that were verified | 120 (56 + 64) | 0 |
| `azure_pages`, `flagged` | 57 | 63 |
| `azure_pages`, `all` | not measured | 94 (41%) |

**Open refinement:** the dealer form's visible CM/ECF header stamp is real embedded text on a page that is otherwise an OCR layer. It is now treated as part of the layer, which is conservative. Separating visible from invisible characters per value would recover it.

**The skill (`skills/ocr/SKILL.md`) is now the entry point for the whole workflow:**
1. scan with `--verify-json --verify-fields all`;
2. send only `azure_pages` to the second OCR service;
3. compare by value;
4. state only agreed values, and quote only agreed sentences;
5. report both readings of any disagreement, and never pick one.

## Fixes from the Azure residual-risk measurement (2026-10-09)

The work-machine measurement ([azure-verify-eval-results.md](azure-verify-eval-results.md), macOS 27) found one value relied on that was really wrong, and four weaknesses. Fixed here:

1. **An amount and its scale word across a line break.** `ocr` already joins `$45` / `million`, but only past one blank line and a pleading number on the same line. On macOS 26 the same page is joined (`$45 million`), so the macOS 27 layout differs; its Markdown is not on this machine yet. The likeliest cause, a line number on a line of its own, is now handled: the join skips line numbers on their own lines (`26`, `26 |`), still at most one blank line between text lines. **To confirm with the macOS 27 bundle.**
2. **A page-end hyphen joined to the footer** (`nonCOMPLAINT`). `ocr` keeps them apart; the joining was in the scoring script. The script now joins a broken word only when the next line starts in lower case, and the skill says a word broken at the foot of a page continues on the next page.
3. **An OCR layer drawn transparent.** ctr-marital-settlement (an iPhone scan, "Created with Scanner Pro") draws its old OCR text in render mode 0 with fill alpha 0, so `ocr_text_layer` missed it and verify trusted 9 values from it. The bridge now also counts text drawn with `ca 0` (and render mode 7) as invisible. New fixture: `spike/fixtures/ocr_layer_alpha.pdf`.
4. **The scoring script was loose** (`eval/azure_verify_eval.py`): it now requires `$ % § ¶` to match (`¶ 60` is not `160`, nor `§ 5` `§§ 1301`), reads U+FFFE as a line-end hyphen, and removes pleading line numbers by position instead of skipping every 1-2 digit token, which hid `¶` misreads.
5. **The skill** says to compare citations with their sign: a `¶` missing or different in either reading is a disagreement. And to compare an amount with its scale word.

**Public filings, `--verify-fields all` (macOS 26):**

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Values verified free | 499 | 490 |
| `azure_pages` | 94 | 109 |
| Pages detected as an OCR layer | 2 filings | 3 filings (+15 pages) |

The 9 values and 15 pages are the marital settlement, now sent to Azure instead of trusted.

**Not fixed:** a docket that PDFKit gives as `5-16-cv-` / `1128` is graded against `5-16-cv-1128`, so `ocr`'s `5-16-cv1128` (letters and digits the same) is a `check`. That is a false alarm, the safe direction.

## Trustworthy measurement (2026-10-09)

From the adversarial review (Notion, "OCR Astra Adversarial Review"), validated against `91c278f`:

- **E03, the blind run was not blind.** `OCR_VERIFY_IGNORE_EMBEDDED=1` hid the embedded text from verify, but the OCR was still corrected from it, so the blind run saw fewer wrong values than a real scan. `eval/verify_eval.py` now reads `truth` and `blind` with `--use-text-layer never` (no correction), and only `truth`'s verify sees the embedded text. A fourth run, `user`, is the scan as users run it, for the headline numbers. Pages whose text is an invisible OCR layer are no longer graded.
- **E04:** `eval/azure_verify_eval.py` confirmed `$1.00` against `$100`. A `.` or `,` between two digits must now be the same.
- **E01:** `eval/score.py` raises on repeated or backward page markers, and counts text before the first marker and on pages the reference lacks as insertions.
- **E02:** token recall is boundary- and occurrence-aware (`$3,000` is not in `$3,000,000`). Transcript-line accuracy is ordered and one-to-one.
- **E06:** `run.py` charges every attempt's wall time. `agg.py` computes throughput only over runs that produced a result, and reports failed runs.

**Rescoring the earlier accept outputs with the new scorer.** CER is unchanged (no output had extra pages):

| Engine | Token recall, old → new | Transcript lines (raw), old → new |
|---|---|---|
| apple (200 DPI) | 95.0% → 94.1% | 38.3% → 28.6% |
| paddleocr-vl | 96.6% → 95.9% | 25.2% → 22.8% |
| dots-ocr | 100% → 100% | 68.1% → 68.1% |
| olmocr | 98.8% → 98.5% | 30.4% → 29.3% |

**New verify baseline** (Apple, `all`, macOS 26, master `91c278f`): 230 pages, 124 graded (embedded text, no OCR layer).

| | Before (half-blind) | Now (blind) |
|---|---|---|
| Graded wrong values in the blind run | 7 | 21 |
| Caught as `check` | 7 | 21 |
| Verified in the blind run | 0 | 0 |

So a real scan has about three times the wrong values the old measurement suggested. All 21 are still caught. As users run it: 490 of 883 values verified, 109 pages to Azure.

## Field instances and signs in `--verify-json` (2026-10-09)

From the adversarial review, findings F01, F02 and F09, all reproduced on master:
- **Swapped values verified.** Embedded `Principal: $8,000. Interest: $3,000.` against OCR `Principal: $3,000. Interest: $8,000.` verified both: the check was "is the value anywhere on the page". So did a value read twice where the page has it once.
- **Signs dropped.** `-$100.00` and `($100.00)` extracted as `$100.00`, and `$100.00` verified against `-$100.00`. The same for `-25%`.
- **Truncation.** `USD 1,00.00` gave a valid `USD 1`, and `§ 1983(A)` lost its subsection.

**Now:**
- Each value in the reference reading backs one OCR value, matched in reading order. It must follow the same label word, one of the two words before it, allowing one misread letter in a long word. Otherwise the value is `check`, with `label_differs` or `more_often_than_in_reference`.
- Minus signs and table accounting brackets are part of the value and its key. Brackets in prose (`Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000.00)`) are not.
- `USD 1,00.00` is `malformed_amount`, and capital subsections are kept.

**Public filings, `all`, macOS 26:**

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Values verified free | 490 | 478 |
| `azure_pages` | 109 | 118 |
| Blind wrong values caught | 21 / 21 | 21 / 21 |

The 12 values that no longer verify:
- 10 are depo-removed-1's running header (docket, date). The OCR misread the header label (`Case:` as `Erik D. Krs`), and PDFKit's text puts the date after `et al.` instead of after the deponent's name.
- 1 is an Ironworkers date with the same reading-order difference.
- 1 is San Bernardino's `$33.5 million`, which the OCR has twice because it repeated a paragraph. Flagging the duplicate is right.

All 12 are false alarms in the safe direction. Taking label words from after a reference value as well would recover them, but it lets a swap through (the next value's label is taken), so it was not done.

**Not changed:** a date at the start of a line (`2 March 2023`) is still not extracted, by design. It is indistinguishable from a pleading line number before `March 2023`.

## Text agreement that keeps numbers (2026-10-09)

From the adversarial review, findings F03 and F10, reproduced on master. Each of these agreed word for word:
- `Payment is $1.00.` against `$100.`;
- `-25%` against `25%`;
- a `30` dropped from `Pay within` / `30` / `days of notice`;
- two sentences in reverse order;
- a sentence read twice where the page has it once.

A value the other reading has and the OCR dropped was never reported.

**Now:**
- In a number, a `.` or `,` between digits, a minus sign and `%` are compared.
- Each word of the other reading backs one sentence, and the sentences of one line agree only in their order. Separate lines may still differ in order (headers, columns).
- A number on a short line of the other reading that the OCR has nowhere is listed in `missing_numbers`, and puts `missing_number` in `page_check`. Only real numbers count: `exhibi1s` is a misread word. A pleading's line numbers (five or more lone numbers) are skipped.
- Values the other reading has and the OCR lacks are listed per page in `expected_fields_missing`. In `all` mode the page gets `fields_missing`.

**Public filings, macOS 26, as users run it:**

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Values verified (`all`) | 478 | 478 |
| `azure_pages`, `all` | 118 | 118 |
| `azure_pages`, `flagged` | 87 | 90 |
| Agreed sentences (`all`, user run) | 6,998 of 9,118 | 6,925 of 9,132 |
| Pages with `missing_number` | – | 40 |
| Pages with `fields_missing` (`all`) | – | 59 |

The blind run still catches 21 of 21 wrong values.

## Second reader and routing (2026-10-09)

From the adversarial review, findings F05, F06 (Bates), F07, A02 and A05:
- **F05:** a date split over two second-reader lines of confidence 0.1 verified, because doubt was decided line by line. Now a value spanning two lines is doubtful if either line is, and a line without confidence counts as doubtful.
- **F06:** on model pages the Bates number comes from Apple's side pass, so the Apple second reading was the same reader again. It no longer verifies Bates numbers.
- **F07:** fallback, engine-flagged and unanchored transcript pages had no `page_check` reason and were never sent to Azure. They now get `engine_fallback`, `engine_flagged` or `line_numbers_unverified`.
- **A02:** a crop that stays empty after its retry while other crops have text now flags the page (Paddle and olmOCR).
- **A05:** a dots reply whose element has a non-string `text` or `category`, or that wraps the array in an object, is incomplete. It is retried, and flagged if it stays so.

**Public filings (Apple):** values verified 478, `azure_pages` 118 (`all`) and 90 (`flagged`), all unchanged. 27 transcript pages now carry `line_numbers_unverified`, but they were already sent. The other changes concern model engines, which were not run for this measurement; unit tests cover them.

## Arithmetic: subtotals and signed amounts (2026-10-09)

From the adversarial review, finding F11, reproduced on master:
- A table with `$10 + $20`, a wrong subtotal `$40`, tax `$5` and total `$45` raised nothing, because a subtotal reset the sum without being checked.
- A refund `($20.00)` was skipped. That gave a false alarm on a correct table with two items, and let a wrong total after a refund pass.
- A mismatch marked only the total's line, though any item above it may be the misread one.

**Now:**
- Subtotals are checked against their items.
- `($20.00)`, `-$20.00` and `$-20.00` count as negative.
- A mismatch marks every amount in the sum (`Mismatch.cells`).

**Measured:**
- **Public filings:** no table triggers it, before or after (478 verified, 118 `azure_pages`).
- **Synthetic `table` family, seeds 10–14:** the same page is flagged before and after (page 2 of each). Only the number of amounts marked on it grows, from the total alone to the whole sum.

## Annotations the renderers never draw (2026-10-09)

From the adversarial review, finding A01, confirmed on master. Both renderers draw page content only (pdfium without annotations or form data, `CGContext.drawPDFPage` on the Mac). So filled form fields, stamps, FreeText amendments, ink and redaction boxes never reach any OCR engine. A probe's filled field `$9,999.00` vanished without a flag. Text under an annotation-style redaction box is still read.

Rendering is unchanged, since that would change every engine's output and needs its own measurement. Pages with annotations that draw something are now flagged instead:
- They get `annotations_not_read` (`annotations_unknown` if the check fails), with the kinds listed in the page's `annotations`.
- They appear in the Markdown's flagged pages and always go to Azure.
- Links, popups and empty form fields are ignored. The pdfium build cannot read form values, so it counts every widget.

**Public filings, macOS 26, as users run it:**

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Values verified | 478 | 459 |
| `azure_pages`, `all` / `flagged` | 118 / 90 | 126 / 98 |
| Pages with `annotations_not_read` | – | 10 |

All 10 are depo-knight-avery, whose pages carry a `watermark` annotation: the filing whose court header stamps Apple misreads and Azure leaves out (docs/azure-verify-eval-results.md). The 19 values that no longer verify are on those pages.

## Where model time goes (2026-10-10, `--timing-json`)

Measured on an M1 Max with a warm server and one request at a time, `--verify-json --verify-fields all`. Four public filings of 10 pages each: cmpl-irhythm, mot-janestreet-opp, depo-knight-avery and scan-dean-habeas. Last night's verification fixes changed no timing: the build before them was within 0.4 s on every document.

| | paddleocr-vl (bf16) | dots-ocr (8-bit) |
|---|---|---|
| Seconds per page | 2.2–3.7 | 7.3–10.9 |
| Requests per page | 1–1.8 (crops) | 1 |
| Prompt tokens per page | about 1,250 | 1,386 |
| Prefill share of request time | 36–59% | 34–48% |
| Prefill speed | about 1,000 tok/s | about 400 tok/s |
| Output tokens per page | 195–540 | 510–960 |
| Decode speed | 250–260 tok/s | about 140 tok/s |
| Retries | none | none |
| Verification per document | 0.1 s (born-digital), 2.6 s (scan) | same |

**What it shows:**
- **Inference is the bottleneck.** Requests take 96–99% of wall time. Page preparation (render, Apple side pass, crop plan: 11–17 s per 10 pages, 44 s on the scan) runs on other threads and is hidden behind inference. It becomes the bottleneck only if inference gets 2–3× faster.
- **Dots spends most of its time decoding layout JSON:** 510–960 tokens per page, much of it bounding boxes and categories, at about 140 tok/s. A text-only prompt (`PROMPT_OCR` exists) could cut decode time sharply, but loses the layout categories the renderer uses.
- **A third or more of the time is prefill of image tokens.** Prompt tokens track image size, so a smaller image or crop costs less. Earlier measurements found higher DPI does not help accuracy.
- **Nothing is retried,** so retry budgets are not where the time goes on these documents.

**Next experiments, in order of expected gain:**
1. Dots text-only mode for pages without tables (measure the accuracy cost).
2. A lower image size per engine.
3. Two requests at once to use spare GPU capacity while decoding. Earlier tries gave 0.91–1.42×, so measure again, with accuracy.

All of them are paired accuracy-and-speed runs on the same pages.

## dots: plain text first (2026-10-10)

`--timing-json` showed dots spending most of its time writing layout JSON: 510–960 output tokens per page at about 140 tok/s. The upstream plain-text prompt (`prompt_ocr`) was already the last fallback. Here it was compared with the layout prompt on the same pages, the same warm server, and alternating order. The layout prompt was used first until now.

**Synthetic fixtures** (ground truth, `eval/score.py`):

| Set | Pages | s/page, layout → plain | Output tokens/page | CER, layout → plain | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pleading, contract, fax, table (seeds 10–12) | 37 | 11.4 / 11.1 / 8.9 / 14.9 → 6.8 / 7.5 / 5.6 / 13.7 | 1,010–1,506 → 258–1,361 | equal or better in every family (fax 6.26% → 0.68%) | token recall 100% both |
| production, seed 10, pages 1–60 | 60 | 7.4 → 5.2 | 513 → 241 | 0.59% → 0.28% | Bates 60/60 both |
| 4-up transcripts (seeds 10–19) | 25 | 37.1 → 14.2 | about 4,100 → 1,190 | 1.29% → 2.10% (pooled) | lines pooled 87.8% → 90.0% (77% → 89% on seeds 10–12, 93.7% → 90.8% on 13–19); recall 100% → 99.7% |

**Public filings** (word error against the PDF's text, 64 pages): plain was 1.3–2.1× faster. Word error went both ways (14.2% → 14.9%, 15.1% → 12.4%, 10.7% → 11.3%), within the noise of reading order.

**Decision:** plain text first on ordinary pages. If the reply is cut off, loops or stays empty, the layout prompt follows (page, then crops), then Apple Vision. A server failure after its retries goes straight to Apple, so a dead server is not asked twice. Transcript pages keep the layout prompt first: plain text was 2.5× faster there but less accurate in two of three measures, and their page:line citations depend on it.

**What plain text loses:** the layout categories, so headings (`#`, `##`), `[Figure]` and formula markers. Tables still come as HTML and are converted. Bates numbers still come from the Apple side pass.

## Lower DPI for the model image: not adopted (2026-10-11)

Prefill (reading the image) is a third or more of each model request, and it grows with image size. The sweep used the same pages, warm servers, rotated order and `--timing-json`.

**Synthetic fixtures** (seeds 10–12 five families, plus production pages 1–60):

| Engine | DPI | s/page, ordinary | CER, ordinary | Production s/page, CER, Bates | 4-up transcripts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dots | 100 (default) | 8.03 | 0.06% | 5.22, 0.28%, 60/60 | CER 2.32%, lines 77.4% |
| dots | 85 | 6.90 | 0.02% | 4.10, 0.16%, 60/60 | CER 2.97%, lines 69.3% |
| dots | 72 | 6.13 | 0.62% | 3.29, 0.25%, **57/60** | CER 10.2%, lines 41.3% |
| paddleocr-vl | 150 (default) | 4.45 | 8.52%* | 2.54, 0.03%, 60/60 | unchanged (crops at 200 DPI) |
| paddleocr-vl | 120 | 4.48 | 0.24%* | 2.34, 0.00%, 60/60 | unchanged |
| paddleocr-vl | 100 | 3.81 | 3.80%*, pleading recall 94.5% | 2.15, 0.00%, 60/60 | unchanged |

\* Paddle's pleading CER swings with DPI (34.6% at 150, 0.8% at 120, 15.3% at 100) while recall stays at 99.5–100%. This is the known margin-number artifact, on 11 pages; it is worth its own look.

- **Paddle:** its image processor resizes the image, so 120 DPI is no faster, and 100 DPI loses words on pleadings. It stays at 150.
- **dots:** 85 DPI looked free on synthetic pages, 14–21% faster. A build that rendered only non-transcript pages at 85 DPI (Apple side pass and transcripts at 100) was then checked on all 20 public filings, 230 pages each way:
  - Overall it was 20% faster: 12.3 → 9.9 s/page.
  - It made real errors that clean synthetic renders do not show:
    - iRhythm page 5 lost a heading and a paragraph, and pages 3–5 read the pleading line numbers as text. Word error rose from 14.9% to 18.0%.
    - The 1985 Lozano typed scan misread words and numbers (`charges` → `fees`, `1963` → `1965`, `Creighton` → `Creston`) and lost a sentence. Word error rose from 59.8% to 66.8%.
    - The Nissan dealer form had a page fall back to Apple.
  - **Not adopted.** dots stays at 100 DPI.

Lesson: synthetic fixtures are clean renders and miss resolution-sensitive failures on real scans. A speed change that lowers image quality must be checked on real filings before it ships.

## dots plain text: a counting run (2026-10-11)

Plain-text-first ("dots: plain text first") was measured on synthetic pages and five public filings. A later run on all 20 public filings found one bad page that those had missed. On cmpl-sec-kuzdas page 5, plain text lost track of the pleading margin:
- it printed the numbers 41 to 100 as bare lines in place of paragraph 22;
- it renumbered paragraph 21 as `37`.

That is a dropped paragraph and a wrong paragraph number. No other public page had a run of 30 or more consecutive bare numbers, in either mode.

Overall word error against the PDF text is the same for both prompts (36.97% layout first against 37.06% plain first, all 20 filings).

**Fix:** a plain reply with more than 28 consecutive bare numbers (a pleading has at most 28 margin numbers) is a bad reply, `counting run`, and goes to the layout prompt like a loop. Re-run on cmpl-sec-kuzdas: page 5's plain reply is rejected (`parse_retry` in `--timing-json`), the layout reply is used, and paragraph 22 and its number are back.

The lesson from "Lower DPI" applies here too: checks on synthetic pages and a few filings did not show this; a full real-filing run did.

## Two model requests at once: not adopted (2026-10-11)

mlx-vlm batches requests continuously (`--max-num-seqs N`), but `ocr` starts it with 1. An experiment build started it with 2 and scanned with `--jobs 2`. The comparison was against 1 and 1, on all 20 public filings (230 pages), with the same warm-server conditions.

| Engine | Wall, 1 → 2 in flight | Speed | Word error against the PDF text | Pages with identical text | Retries |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| paddleocr-vl | 1,332 s → 1,594 s | 0.84× | 36.87% → 40.00% | 128 of 230 | 11 restarts after timeouts with 2 in flight, none with 1 |
| dots-ocr | 5,010 s → 8,466 s | 0.59× | 36.92% → 43.38% | 46 of 230 | 43 bad-reply retries and 17 restarts with 2, against 4 and 4 with 1 |

**Two in flight is slower and less accurate on both engines.** Batching changes the outputs: most dots pages differ, and its replies loop or break more often. The timeouts then trigger server restarts, which the client handles as if it were the only request running (review finding P05). That is consistent with the earlier MLX finding (0.91–1.42×, Paddle bf16 slower at 2).

dots one at a time was slower in this run than in the DPI check the day before (21.8 s against 12.3 s per page, with 4 restarts). Part of this run overlapped other work on the machine. The comparison was made under the same conditions, and the result does not depend on it.

**Not adopted:** the server stays at one request at a time. The remaining speed levers are the per-page choices already made (plain text first for dots) and engine choice.

## Filing-stamp values and two image readers (2026-10-11)

`eval/verify_eval.py` on paddleocr-vl (20 public filings, scan conditions: the blind run hides the PDF text) found 10 wrongly verified values:
- **8 were the Jane Street filing stamp.** `04/24/24` is printed over `04/18/24`, and Paddle and the Apple second reading both read it as `04/28/24`, so their agreement verified the wrong date on every page.
- **1 was a paragraph-sign count** (`¶ 8-10` for `¶¶ 8-10`).
- **1 was a grading artifact** (the PDF text glues a footnote marker to `$1,000,000`).

**Fix:** values on the court's electronic filing stamp line (`Case … Document … Filed … Page … of …`) are never verified by the second image reader. They get `court_stamp` and stay unconfirmed until the PDF's own text or Azure agrees. The PDF's own text still verifies them on born-digital pages.

| Paddle, 20 filings | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Blind values verified | 461 | 295 |
| ...of which wrong | 10 (2.2%) | 2 (0.7%; one sign count, one grading artifact) |
| Wrong values caught as `check` | 4 of 14 | 12 of 14 |
| Values verified as users run it | 721 of 1,097 | 629 |
| `azure_pages` | 125 | 138 |

The values that no longer verify are the filing-stamp docket, date and page numbers repeated on every scanned page. Apple-only runs are unaffected: two Apple readings never verify each other.

## The human-checked holdout set, v1 (2026-10-12)

`eval/holdout/holdout_v1.json` covers 18 public filings and 61 pages (`docs/holdout-plan.md`). It was reviewed by Patrick in the review page, with the pre-fill from Apple on his work Mac. Values his notes named, and values other engines or the PDF's own text found that the pre-fill had missed, were checked against the page images and confirmed with him. The set holds **292 values and 12 transcribed pages**. Page facts were not reviewed in v1.

Two decisions are recorded in the set:
- a docket is compared by court office, year, type and number, without judge initials;
- the pre-fill's two "Bates" values `WA 98104` were ZIP codes and are excluded.

`eval/holdout/score.py` compares an engine's output by typed value, with its own parser.

**Baseline** (master `e08094d` plus PRs 35–37, macOS 26, `--verify-json --verify-fields all`):

| Engine | Values found | Verified but wrong | Amounts | Dates | Dockets | Transcription CER / word error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apple | 83.6% | **0** | 46/71 | 134/151 | 46/49 | 14.3% / 20.7% |
| paddleocr-vl | 88.4% | **0** | 50/71 | 140/151 | 48/49 | 17.2% / 23.6% |
| dots-ocr | 67.5% | **0** | 53/71 | 105/151 | 19/49 | 29.9% / 38.0% |

- **No engine verified a wrong value.** Every verified value is on the page.
- **What is missed:**
  - dates in capitals (`MARCH 15, 2007`);
  - invoice amounts without a `$` next to them;
  - stamps (struck-through or overprinted filing headers, RECEIVED stamps);
  - handwriting.
- **dots finds 19 of 49 dockets.** Most dockets are in the court's filing-stamp header, which the plain-text prompt (adopted in "dots: plain text first") appears to leave out. This is to be checked.

## Extraction gaps found by the holdout set (2026-10-12)

The holdout set showed four extraction gaps in `ocr` (values missed, none wrongly verified). Each was copied into the development tests and fixed there:
1. **Dates in capitals:** `MARCH 15, 2007`, `TUESDAY, MARCH 13, 1990`, `APR 15 2008`. Month names, ordinals and "day of" now match in any case.
2. **Invoice amounts without `$`:** these are now money:
   - a number grouped with cents (`5,156.00`), anywhere;
   - a number with cents in a table column headed by a money word (amount, rate, fee, total, balance, due, and so on). Not under a quantity word such as hours or units;
   - a line of nothing but such numbers within six lines below a `$` or a money word.

   Accounting brackets in a money column are negative.
3. **ZIP codes as Bates numbers:** a state abbreviation and a 5-digit ZIP (`WA 98104`) is no longer a Bates number.
4. **Leader dots in citations:** `§ 1692.....12` is `§ 1692`.

**Results:**

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Holdout, Apple: values found (292) | 83.6% | 93.3% |
| Holdout, Apple: verified but wrong | 0 | 0 |
| Public filings (`all`): values found | 883 | 899 |
| Public filings: verified | 459 | 464 |
| Public filings: `azure_pages` | 126 | 126 |
| Public filings: blind wrong values caught | 21 of 21 | 18 of 18 |

Seven values the fixes found on the holdout set were confirmed by the PDFs' own text and added to the set: h02 `JANUARY 8, 2010`, h06 `0.00`, and h09's balance column.

What Apple still misses on the holdout set is mostly stamps, struck-through headers, handwriting and text it did not read at all.

## dots: the filing-stamp header put back (2026-10-12)

The holdout set showed dots finding only 19 of 49 dockets. Since "dots: plain text first", dots often leaves out the court's colored filing-stamp header (`Case … Document … Filed … Page … of …`). That header holds the case number, filed date and page count; on h05 its case number differs from the caption's.

**Fix:** when the Apple side pass reads a filing-stamp line at the top of a model page (top tenth), and the model's text has no such line, Apple's line is put at the top of the page. Its values still get `court_stamp`, so two image readers never verify them; the PDF's own text or Azure can.

**Holdout, dots, against master:** values found 74.3% → 85.3% (dockets 19 → 34 of 49, dates 113 → 130 of 151), verified but wrong 0 → 0.

## Holdout re-score on the v1.0 release build (2026-10-18)

Release build of master `3dff738` (`cargo build --release`, `ocr 0.2.0`), macOS 26.6.2 on an M1 Max (32 GB), `eval/holdout/prepare.py scan` (`--verify-json --verify-fields all`), scored with `eval/holdout/score.py`. Paddle is PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 bf16, dots is dots.mocr 8bit, both on mlx-vlm 0.7.6.

| Engine | Values found (292) | Verified but wrong | Verified / check | Amounts | Dates | Dockets | Citations | CER / word error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apple | 93.5% (2026-10-12: 93.3%) | **0** | 141 / 132 | 67/71 | 142/151 | 46/49 | 16/19 | 14.3% / 20.7% |
| paddleocr-vl | 96.6% (baseline: 88.4%) | **0** | 181 / 101 | 67/71 | 146/151 | 48/49 | 19/19 | 17.5% / 23.8% |
| dots-ocr | 85.3% (2026-10-12: 85.3%) | **0** | 175 / 74 | 65/71 | 130/151 | 34/49 | 18/19 | 28.1% / 36.4% |

- **The bar holds: no engine marked a wrong value `verified`.** No engine value outside the set was verified either (Apple 4, Paddle 3, dots 5 extra values, all `check`).
- **Misreads were all `check`:** Apple `2:21-cy-00598` (h05) and `March 24, 2002` (h12), Paddle and dots `March 24, 2001` (h12, truth `March 24, 2008`).
- Paddle's gain since its baseline comes from the extraction fixes of 2026-10-12 (dates in capitals, amounts without `$`); it had not been re-scored since.
- dots still drops 15 of 49 dockets and 21 dates, mostly the filing-stamp header on old scans (h03, h12, h13) and the pleading caption docket on h14.

### indra-ocr on the Mac (2026-10-18)

First real run of indra-ocr on macOS (it had been tested only with the fake helper). Setup failed at first: Datalab squashed the Hugging Face repo's history on 2026-10-15, removing the pinned revision `5993a95` (404). The pin is now `ed345c7`; all seven files have the same sha256.

- Setup (uv venv, seven weight files, checksums) took 5 s.
- Scans worked on scanned and born-digital PDFs, `--use-text-layer always`, PNG, a page rotated 90° (read upright) and a two-page TIFF.
- The verify second reader applies: on h01, both values were verified by the Vision re-read.
- A run stopped with SIGTERM after 102 of 500 pages resumed from the checkpoints to the same output as a clean run. The helper exits about a second after `ocr` is killed, even with SIGKILL.
- 500-page production at 300 DPI, one thread: 5.4 pages/s on the M1 Max.

**Holdout:** values found 66.8%, **verified but wrong 0** (142 verified, 53 check; amounts 65/71, dates 96/151, dockets 14/49, citations 18/19; CER 23.1%, word error 39.9%). Its one misread, `March 24, 2001` (h12), is `check`. Most of what it drops is the court's filing stamp, which indra classifies as a page header and `ocr` leaves out of the body, as dots did before 2026-10-12.

**Fix:** a header or footer block that is the filing stamp (`COURT_STAMP`) is put back at the top of the page, after the Bates search (so its `Page 2 of 5` is never a Bates number). Its values keep `court_stamp`, so the Vision re-read never verifies them. Tests: three `page_result` unit tests and a fake-helper scan with `--verify-json` (`INDRA_FAKE_STAMP`).

**Holdout, indra-ocr:** values found 66.8% → **80.8%** (dockets 14 → 34 of 49, dates 96 → 117 of 151), verified 142 → 164, **verified but wrong 0 → 0**. Of the values on restored stamp lines, 24 are verified by the PDF's own text and none by the Vision re-read; 11 are `check` with `court_stamp`.

### olmOCR on the holdout set (2026-10-18)

olmOCR 2 (mlx-community 8bit), build of #46, same settings. 61 pages took 28 minutes (about 28 s a page on the M1 Max).

| Values found (292) | Verified but wrong | Verified / check | Amounts | Dates | Dockets | Citations | CER / word error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 77.4% | **0** | 160 / 66 | 61/71 | 113/151 | 31/49 | 19/19 | 28.7% / 27.6% |

- No misreads: every value olmOCR found is the page's. No engine value outside the set was verified (3 extra, all `check`).
- What it drops is mostly filing-stamp dates and dockets on old scans (h03, h11, h12), the capitalised header date on h10 (`MARCH 15, 2007`) and h10's invoice amounts.
- The lowest word error of all engines (27.6%) but a high CER: it drops whole header and footer lines.

### indra-ocr 1.1.2 upgrade (Linux, 2026-10-22)

No Mac was available. Same machine as the Linux synthetic runs (32 logical CPUs, AMD Ryzen 9 9950X). The 0.3.1 Mac holdout above is history.

- **Setup.** `ocr server setup --model indra-ocr` against a stale install finished in 13 s and recorded `indra-ocr 1.1.2` (`datalab-to/indra-ocr@a1283c4`). The isolated eval state installed the same pin (twelve weight files, about 76 MB on disk as decimal MB).
- **Speed.** `spike/fixtures/legal_scan.pdf` (1 page): 0.8–0.9 s (about 1.1 pages/s), including model load. Accept seeds 10–12, model loaded each file: 0.7–1.5 pages/s. One 20-page production file: 4.5 pages/s (4.5 s wall). A 3-page pleading: 1.8 pages/s.
- **Memory.** Helper peak 0.6 GB on the pleading and the 20-page production file, 0.9 GB on a 3-page 4-up transcript. `ocr` process peak on the accept seeds was 543–843 MB. No server.
- **Accuracy.** Synthetic and holdout numbers are in docs/eval.md and the README. No `[Figure]` text in either set, so the CER change from 0.3.1 is not the picture-placeholder rewrite.
